title: Tile Families for the Discrete Carleson Theorem

aux𝓒.statement: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, we define an auxiliary collection $\operatorname{aux}\mathcal{C}(k)$ of dyadic cubes, a subset of $\mathcal{D}$ (the grid of $X$).

dens'.statement: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a set of tiles $\mathfrak{P}' \subseteq \mathfrak{P}(X)$, we define the density $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\mathfrak{P}') \in [0, \infty]$ as in (5.1.6).

ℭ.statement: For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the set of tiles $\mathfrak{C}(k, n) \subseteq \mathfrak{P}(X)$; these sets form the partition of $\mathfrak{P}(k)$ by density given in (5.1.7).

𝔐.statement: For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the set of tiles $\mathfrak{M}(k, n) \subseteq \mathfrak{P}(X)$ as in (5.1.4) and (5.1.5).

𝔅.statement: For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a tile $p \in \mathfrak{P}(X)$, we define the subset $\mathfrak{B}(p)$ of $\mathfrak{M}(k, n)$ as in (5.1.8).

ℭ₁.statement: For $k, n, j \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the subset $\mathfrak{C}_1(k, n, j)$ of $\mathfrak{C}(k, n)$ as in (5.1.9). Together with $\mathfrak{L}_0(k, n)$ these sets form a partition (of $\mathfrak{C}(k,n)$).

ℭ₂.statement: For $k, n, j \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the subset $\mathfrak{C}_2(k, n, j)$ of $\mathfrak{C}_1(k, n, j)$ as in (5.1.13).

𝔘₁.statement: For $k, n, j \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the subset $\mathfrak{U}_1(k, n, j)$ of $\mathfrak{C}_1(k, n, j)$ as in (5.1.14).

ℭ₅.statement: For $k, n, j \in \mathbb{N}$, we define the subset $\mathfrak{C}_5(k, n, j)$ of $\mathfrak{C}_4(k, n, j)$ as in (5.1.23).
